title: K3 Surfaces from the Lattice Up — a textbook with a verified core (edition 0.1)
description:
A textbook on K3 surfaces built from the arithmetic of integral lattices upward, for a reader with linear algebra, a first course in complex analysis and the vocabulary of algebraic geometry, who wants to reach the point where the transcendental lattice of a K3 surface, the monodromy of a Picard–Fuchs equation and the geometry of a modular curve meet.

Chapters. 1 Integral lattices (Gram matrices, discriminant forms, orthogonal complements and the index formula, Nikulin's theorems; worked examples U⊕⟨2N⟩, E8, the K3 lattice, and the binary forms A2, ⟨2⟩⊕⟨2⟩, [[2,1],[1,4]]). 2 K3 surfaces (definition, Hodge diamond, Néron–Severi and transcendental lattices, Picard number 20, the ample cone). 3 Periods, Torelli and lattice polarizations (period domain, global Torelli, surjectivity, Dolgachev's Mn-polarized families, the modular group inside the isometry group). 4 Elliptic fibrations (Kodaira's classification, Tate's algorithm, Shioda–Tate, the Inose pencil with exact orders of vanishing). 5 Picard–Fuchs equations (variation of Hodge structure, Doran's symmetric-square theorem and its converse, Apéry-like and Cooper sequences). 6 Singular K3 surfaces and complex multiplication (Shioda–Inose structures, rank jumps along a family, the walls of T7 and T10). 7 Modular curves and the Fricke involution (Γ0(n)+, Atkin–Lehner, Hauptmoduln, the dictionary between modular curve, lattice and surface). 8 The frontier: Cooper's sporadic operators and the M7-polarized family, every claim marked. 9 What “kernel-checked” means. Exercises in every chapter with hints.

Status convention. Every statement carries a mark: (L) literature, quoted with a precise citation; (E) exact computation the reader can rerun; (N) numerical evidence; (K) kernel-checked in Lean 4 with the three standard axioms only, in the public repository SocrateAI-DualScaleTopologicalUniverseModel-LeanProposal. The (K) core is the lattice arithmetic of Chapter 1: the exact orthogonal complements of five classes in U⊕⟨14⟩ and U⊕⟨20⟩, including the integral isometry U⊕⟨14⟩ ≅ ⟨−2⟩ ⊕ [[2,1],[1,4]]. No physics is discussed.

Provenance. Drafted with the assistance of an AI model (Claude, Fable 5.1) inside the repository holding the Lean development; kernel-checked statements are transcribed from a stated commit; literature statements are the author's responsibility. Edition 0.1, 29 September 2026.
